summary: The study investigates the atomic layer deposition (ALD) of Al2O3 using trimethylaluminum (TMA) and water at 125 °C. The research focuses on the growth behavior, self-limiting nature, and surface reactions during ALD. The results show that the ALD process is not completely self-limiting at lower temperatures, requiring longer exposure times for reactions to complete. The study also explores the relationship between hydroxyl coverage, methyl coverage, and the mass gain per cycle (MGPC) during ALD.
evidence: Al2O3 atomic layer deposition (ALD) growth with Al(CH3)3 (trimethylaluminum (TMA)) and H2O as the reactants was examined at the relatively low temperature of 125 °C using quartz crystal microbalance (QCM) measurements. The Al2O3 MGPCs increased with increasing H2O and TMA exposures at fixed TMA and H2O exposures, respectively. However, the TMA and H2O reactions were not completely self-limiting. The slower surface reaction kinetics at lower temperature may require very long exposures for the reactions to reach completion.
